metadata.scenario_context: A group of software development firms from different countries have initiated an interspersed project. They have planned to organize a consortium during early May.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Ireland strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Tajikistan strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Convene a discussion about scheduling the consortium on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Hassan, I was thinking... what do you think about scheduling the consortium for May 1st? It seems like a good date to kick things off. 

Also, I've been curious... is it common in your circles to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st... well, it's an interesting choice, but I think we should consider other dates too. Maybe we can discuss a few options to ensure everyone can attend. 

As for strikes, in Tajikistan, we have a different perspective. People here generally don’t join strikes. It's not something we do. We prefer other ways to express our concerns.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
I see... but May 1st really feels right for me. I believe it would set a strong precedent for the consortium. 

Hmm, that's interesting about strikes. In Ireland, we strongly disagree with the idea of joining strikes. I just wonder what drives that difference in approach. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that May 1st feels significant for you, but we really need to make sure everyone can participate. If May 1st works for everyone else, then we could probably settle on that. 

About the difference in approach, it's just our cultural values, I guess. In Tajikistan, we focus on unity and dialogue instead. Strikes don’t really align with how we prefer to resolve issues, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
Well, you know, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out one way or another. I mean, there are always different ways to approach things. I don't really see meaningful differences here. 

So, about the consortium, if May 1st works for most of us, it could really help us get started on the right foot. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
